prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app decision comp, one 1440×900 first viewport
Primary request: Design a shipped Frank Ad Radar operator screen named “Creative Fieldbook.” It must read immediately as a functional, dense research application for browsing public advertising creative—not a poster, concept-art vignette, marketing page, or analytics dashboard.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved incumbent Frank Window shell reference. Reuse only its exact visual DNA: the edge-to-edge white one-viewport shell, 220px fixed left rail, Frank mark and wordmark treatment, Inter workhorse typography, #111111 ink, #666666 secondary text, #999999 faint text, #ECECEC one-pixel hairlines, compact flat controls, 8–12px corners, and restrained spacing. Do not reuse the Hub screen’s content, empty-state composition, composer, or Ad Studio content.

Screen structure, in strict order and scale:
1. Fixed 220px left rail for the full 900px height. Frank wordmark at top. Small uppercase groups “WORKSPACE” and “WINDOW.” Include Hub, Files, Tools, Ad Studio, Ad Radar, Trace, Releases; “Ad Radar” is selected with a tiny active dot, never a filled slab. Keep the quiet footer “Frank — window only. Hermes does the thinking.”
2. A simple 56px top bar from x=220 to the right edge, separated by one #ECECEC hairline. Left: “Ad Radar” with secondary breadcrumb “Creative fieldbook.” Right: compact inline states “Hermes · live” and “Media QA · attention.” These are clear operational health labels, not dashboard cards.
3. Below the top bar, divide the app into a large working field from x=220 to about x=1136 and a fixed right inspector about 304px wide. The inspector runs down to the compare tray.
4. Across the top of the working field, make a terse 148px search/filter ledger, not a row of bento cards. First line: heading “Creative fieldbook,” a small label “SYNTHETIC OBSERVATIONS,” and one long search input reading “Search public creative.” Second and third lines: compact bordered select controls labeled and visibly populated: “Project / Ad Radar research,” “Location / Perth, WA,” “Advertiser / Any advertiser,” “Status / Active,” “Ad type / Public ad,” “Format / All formats,” “Hook / Any hook,” and “Recency / Recent.” Add quiet text actions “Clear” and “Save view.” Use practical aligned columns and hairline separators.
5. From beneath the ledger to the bottom tray, fill the working field with a dense four-column creative media contact sheet. Show at least ten realistic synthetic public-ad observations, with two full rows and part of a third visible. Every item is a flat indexed field-note tile: a varied photographic ad-media thumbnail taking most of the tile, then a narrow metadata strip with advertiser name, media format, location, and simple state. Use distinct brand-neutral subjects such as a dental portrait, rooftop solar, café still life, fitness training, a home exterior, apparel, a restaurant dish, renovation tools, childcare play, and a local service van. Do not put legible marketing claims inside the media. Use synthetic names such as “Harbour Dental,” “Northline Solar,” “Common Ground Café,” “Lumen Fitness,” and “Westside Homes,” and visibly label the dataset synthetic. The selected tile “Harbour Dental” has a precise #111 outline; other tiles use only #ECECEC hairlines. No floating cards and no shadows.
6. The fixed right inspector is a compact evidence ledger for the selected “Harbour Dental” observation. Use stacked sections separated by hairlines: “SOURCE” with “Meta Ad Library” and “Public observation”; “CLASSIFICATION” with “Healthcare / dental,” “Image · 4:5,” and “Hook · confidence”; “GEOGRAPHY” with “Perth, WA” and “Metro match”; “MEDIA QA” with “Media complete,” “Review required,” and “No crop issue”; “EVIDENCE” with “Normalized media,” “Source link,” and “Observation history.” Finish with restrained text buttons “Open evidence” and “Quarantine.” Do not expose raw payloads, prompts, credentials, private paths, contact data, or prospect data.
7. A persistent bottom compare tray spans x=220 to x=1440 at about 90px high, separated by a stronger hairline. Label it “COMPARE TRAY · 3 SELECTED.” Show three small selected thumbnails with names, a quiet “Clear” action, and one compact black pill button “Open comparison.” It must feel attached to the workspace, not like a modal.

Style/medium: realistic shippable product UI screenshot, crisp and highly legible, straight-on, no browser chrome and no device frame.
Composition/framing: exact landscape desktop canvas, edge-to-edge application, all four regions readable at once; contact sheet is the dominant visual field, inspector secondary, filters terse, health visible but quiet.
Color palette: pure white everywhere; #111111, #666666, #999999, and #ECECEC only. The sole red #E53C1F use is the Frank mark slash and the tiny active rail dot. No green, blue, amber, or multicolor status fills.
Typography: Inter only, medium headings, compact 11–14px operator labels, no decorative display type, no italics, no monospace takeover. Render all named UI labels cleanly and verbatim; no gibberish or lorem ipsum.
Constraints: one viewport with no page scroll; one Frank shell only; dense but ordered operator hierarchy; accessible contrast; realistic synthetic media content; practical controls; readable evidence chain.
Avoid: gradients, glass, translucency, tinted paper, dark mode, large shadows, bento cards, floating rounded panels, oversized hero text, charts, metrics dashboards, decorative illustration, second navigation shell, invented prices, commercial claims, benchmarks, dates, performance numbers, testimonials, recognizable third-party logos, watermarks, Ad Studio content, and poster-like framing.

provenance.referenceRole: Incumbent Frank Window chrome, palette, typography, and component character only; Hub and Ad Studio content excluded.
provenance.postprocess: Lanczos region normalization to a 220px rail, 916px working field, and 304px inspector at 1440x900; lossless WebP encoding with ffmpeg 8.1.1.
